# Hermes Agent: Onboarding FAQ & Guide

### 1. Platforms, Docker & Web Interface

**Q: Is native Windows supported?**  
Yes. Windows 10/11 is Tier 1 supported via `install.ps1`. For the dashboard's embedded terminal chat (`/chat`), WSL2 is recommended due to POSIX PTY requirements.

**Q: Does Docker support ARM64 / Raspberry Pi / Apple Silicon?**  
Yes. Official images (`nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest`) support multi-arch (`linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`). For NAS permissions (UGOS, Synology, unRAID) on mapped `/opt/data`, set `PUID` and `PGID` (or `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID`) env vars.

**Q: Can I run Hermes on Android via Termux?**  
Yes. `install.sh` detects Termux, uses `$TMPDIR`, and installs the curated `[termux-all]` bundle.

**Q: Is there a Web UI?**  
Yes. Run `hermes dashboard` to launch the local web UI at `http://127.0.0.1:9119` with an embedded chat interface.

---

### 2. Providers, Models & Connectivity

**Q: Why are local models (Ollama/Qwen 4B–9B) slow?**  
Hermes sends ~45 tool schemas on every turn, causing high prompt-token load for small models. To optimize: disable unused tools via `hermes tools`, use faster quantizations or larger models (32B+), and set `terminal.backend: local`.

**Q: Why does Hermes ignore my local `base_url`?**  
`provider: auto` picks up remote env vars (e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). Set `provider: custom` with `base_url: http://localhost:11434` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.

**Q: How do I use Claude Pro/Max subscriptions instead of API tokens?**  
Claude API keys always bill per-token. Authenticate via Claude OAuth to use Pro/Max subscription quotas.

**Q: How do I connect Azure AI Foundry or Ollama Cloud?**  
- **Azure AI Foundry**: Set `provider: azure-foundry` and `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL` (or run `hermes setup`).
- **Ollama Cloud**: Set provider to `ollama-cloud` (routes to `https://ollama.com/v1`).

**Q: Can I enable vision on custom/Ollama models?**  
Set `supports_vision: true` in your model configuration.

**Q: Does Hermes support automatic smart model routing?**  
No. Automatic complexity/cost-based routing (`smart_model_routing`) was removed by policy. Switch manually (`/model`, `hermes chat -m <model>`) or configure subagents via `delegation.model`.

**Q: Why does Gemini CLI OAuth fail?**  
Google bans third-party tools using CLI OAuth. Use Google AI Studio with `GOOGLE_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY` or Vertex AI instead.

---

### 3. Messaging Gateways & Personas

**Q: How do I configure Discord, Telegram, or other gateways?**  
Run `hermes gateway setup` for an interactive wizard to configure tokens and user permissions.

**Q: Why does Telegram say "Unauthorized user"?**  
`allowed_chats` is only a group filter. Authorize your user ID in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:
```yaml
telegram:
  allow_from: "YOUR_TELEGRAM_USER_ID"  # or allow_all: true
```
Or approve DM pairing codes with `hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>`.

**Q: Can gateways handle files and images?**  
Yes. Inbound text/code (`.txt`, `.py`) is injected or cached. Outbound files route to platform delivery (Matrix `m.file`, Email attachments, DingTalk Markdown `![image](url)`, Telegram media). MCP tool image results (`MEDIA:<path>`) are also forwarded.

**Q: Can I run per-channel personas or multi-agent workflows?**  
- **Per-Channel Persona**: Set `channel_prompts` per channel ID in platform configs.
- **Profiles**: Run multiplexed gateways to isolate credentials, skills, memory, and sessions per account.
- **Subagents**: Use `delegate_task` to spawn child `AIAgent` instances.

---

### 4. Memory, Skills & Execution

**Q: What are `SOUL.md`, `USER.md`, and `MEMORY.md`?**  
- `SOUL.md`: Agent persona, character, and core guidelines.
- `USER.md`: Persistent user preferences/profile (`target="user"`).
- `MEMORY.md`: Long-term factual agent memory.

**Q: Can I add custom memory providers or custom tools?**  
In-tree additions to `plugins/memory/` are closed. Create external plugins implementing `MemoryProvider` or register tools with `ctx.register_tool` in `~/.hermes/plugins/`, then enable with `hermes plugins enable <name>`. Local Honcho servers work without API keys.

**Q: What happens at the tool-call limit?**  
`agent.max_turns` defaults to 90 (`hermes chat --max-turns <N>`). When reached, Hermes completes the turn without tools. For long autonomous jobs, use `/goal <task>` (Ralph loop), which persists across turns and resumes with `/goal resume`.

**Q: How do session resets and recovery work?**  
Crashes/restarts preserve state under `resume_pending`. Use `/resume` to restore transcripts. Unconfigured session resets default to `mode: none`.

---

### 5. Diagnostics & Observability

- **Diagnostics**: Run `hermes doctor` to verify Python environment, configs, and provider credentials.
- **Skill Telemetry**: Track skill executions using `/insights` or `hermes insights` (`~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json`).
- **Tracing**: Enable Langfuse call-chain tracing via `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse`.
- **Update Note**: If `hermes update` pauses on Node dependencies, Camofox is downloading browser binaries.
- **Security**: Report vulnerabilities privately to `security@nousresearch.com` or via GitHub Security Advisories.
